tasks.title: Use POSIX-millisecond timestamps in RateUpdate schedules
tasks.description:
## Context

RealFi v1.2 RC1 represents protocol time on Cardano as absolute POSIX milliseconds:

- staking-vault `diffusion_start` and `diffusion_end`;
- transaction validity bounds used by `diffusion_rate_time`;
- unstake-lock `unlock_time`.

The recently merged EVM rate-schedule implementation instead converts those timestamps at the producer boundary to Shelley-relative Cardano slots, then converts the slots back to Unix seconds in `RealFiRateReceiver` using deployment-specific `cardanoSystemStart` and `cardanoSlotLength` values.

That conversion is unnecessary and introduces another clock representation, a single-era slot-anchor assumption, deployment configuration, and avoidable precision loss. No production Cardano rate-schedule publisher has been identified yet, so this is the right point to align the wire contract with the canonical Cardano representation.

This follows realfi-cross-chain-spine#16 and realfi#1564.

## Decision

Represent both `RateUpdate` schedule endpoints as absolute POSIX milliseconds.

Keep the RFC1 header and the 120-byte hook length unchanged. The revised hook is unsigned, fixed-width, and big-endian:

| Offset | Size | Field |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 0 | 8 | monotonic `sequence` (`uint64`) |
| 8 | 8 | absolute `originTimeMs` (`uint64`) |
| 16 | 32 | settled USDr `startBacking` (`uint256`) |
| 48 | 32 | settled USDr `targetBacking` (`uint256`) |
| 80 | 32 | constant sUSDr `shareSupply` (`uint256`) |
| 112 | 8 | absolute `targetTimeMs` (`uint64`) |

`amount` remains `floor(targetBacking * 1e18 / shareSupply)`.

On EVM, evaluate the schedule at:

```text
nowMs = block.timestamp * 1000
```

No fixed-length staking epoch is implied. Schedule origin, target, native-staking cutoff, freshness, and admission-generation transitions are independent explicit values.

Future authenticated native-staking configuration should use the same time coordinate for its explicit `cutoffTimeMs`.

## Required changes

### Solidity codec and receiver

- Rename the `originSlot` / `targetSlot` readers and fields to `originTimeMs` / `targetTimeMs`.
- Remove slot-to-Unix conversion from `RealFiRateReceiver`.
- Evaluate interpolation and future-origin checks in milliseconds.
- Keep `staleness` and `maxScheduleWindow` externally denominated in seconds if desired, converting them to milliseconds at comparison sites.
- Remove `cardanoSystemStart` and `cardanoSlotLength` from new deployment configuration.
- If an existing UUPS storage layout must be preserved, retain the old storage slots as deprecated rather than reordering or deleting them.

### Producer and Cardano tooling

- Build the Cardano rate-schedule producer so that `targetTimeMs` is copied from the vault POSIX-ms `diffusion_end`, while `originTimeMs` is the exact Cardano POSIX-ms observation point used to derive `startBacking`; perform no slot conversion. For a newly installed window that observation may equal `diffusion_start`; for a later broadcast or rebase during an active window it is the later observation time.
- Update Aiken and Haskell `RateUpdateHook` names/types and typed encoders for schema parity.
- Do not convert Cardano validity time to a slot when constructing `RateUpdate`.

The Aiken vault datum and diffusion arithmetic already use POSIX milliseconds and require no mathematical change.

### Vectors, tests, and documentation

- Regenerate the authoritative EVM vectors and vendor them into `realfi-cross-chain-spine`.
- Update codec, staking, integration, delayed-delivery, freshness, and schedule-window tests.
- Include endpoints with non-zero millisecond components so an accidental seconds-or-slot interpretation cannot pass.
- Remove the Shelley-anchor requirements from the schedule documentation and deployment runbook.

## Compatibility and rollout

Although the encoded length is unchanged, this is a wire-semantic change. Producer and receiver upgrades must be coordinated.

The mismatch fails closed in both directions:

- an old receiver interprets POSIX milliseconds as a far-future slot and rejects the update;
- a new receiver interprets an old Shelley-relative slot as a timestamp near 1970 and rejects it as stale.

Do not publish the new format until every target receiver accepts it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Cardano diffusion state, RFC1 `RateUpdate`, and EVM schedule evaluation use absolute POSIX milliseconds at the protocol boundary.
- The 120-byte hook is encoded and decoded byte-for-byte across Solidity, Haskell, Aiken schema tooling, and spine vectors.
- EVM interpolation reproduces Cardano backing-first floor rounding at the same whole-second observation points.
- Delayed delivery does not shift either schedule endpoint.
- Future, stale, immediate-loss, active-window, target-boundary, and maximum-window tests pass.
- New deployments require no Cardano system-start or slot-length configuration for rate schedules.
- Conformance vectors contain non-second-aligned millisecond endpoints.

tasks.title: RFC1 parity: re-vendor 120-byte RateUpdate and 64-byte StakeRoute vectors into v1_2_rc1 cctp.ak
tasks.description:
## Context

Target branch: **v1_2_beta**. The obsolete cross-chain-state branch is not in scope.

The V1.2 RC1 Aiken RFC1 implementation has drifted from the EVM-authoritative codec vectors:

- [contracts/lib/v1_2_rc1/cctp.ak on v1_2_beta](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/blob/v1_2_beta/contracts/lib/v1_2_rc1/cctp.ak) still models RateUpdate as the old 16-byte sequence + origin-slot hook and accepts hook lengths greater than or equal to 16.
- [contracts/lib/v1_2_rc1/cctp.tests.ak on v1_2_beta](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/blob/v1_2_beta/contracts/lib/v1_2_rc1/cctp.tests.ak) still pins the obsolete 16-byte RateUpdate message/digest (e91f63a8...).
- StakeRoute has the finalized 64-byte shares + effective-rate shape, but its Aiken test uses a separately constructed example instead of the exact authoritative EVM vector and attestation digest.
- The authoritative source is [eth/hardhat/test/vectors/cctp-message-vectors.json on v1_2_beta](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/blob/v1_2_beta/eth/hardhat/test/vectors/cctp-message-vectors.json), documented in [CODEC-VECTORS.md](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/blob/v1_2_beta/eth/hardhat/docs/CODEC-VECTORS.md).

## Dependency and wire-format warning

Blocked on [#1567 — Use POSIX-millisecond timestamps in RateUpdate schedules](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/issues/1567).

The currently committed EVM RateUpdate vector is already 120 bytes, but still names and interprets its endpoints as Shelley-relative slots. Do not make that slot-based vector the final Aiken fixture. Once #1567 lands and regenerates the authoritative vectors, re-vendor the resulting 120-byte POSIX-ms vector byte-for-byte.

The final RateUpdate hook is:

| Offset | Size | Field |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 0 | 8 | sequence |
| 8 | 8 | originTimeMs |
| 16 | 32 | startBacking |
| 48 | 32 | targetBacking |
| 80 | 32 | shareSupply |
| 112 | 8 | targetTimeMs |

The finalized StakeRoute hook is exactly 64 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Field |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 0 | 32 | susdrShares |
| 32 | 32 | effectiveRate |

## Work

- Update V1.2 RC1 RateUpdateHook and decode_rate_update_hook in cctp.ak to the final 120-byte POSIX-ms schema.
- Require the canonical exact hook length of 120 bytes.
- Preserve the finalized exact 64-byte StakeRoute decoder and pricing relation.
- Re-vendor the exact RateUpdate and StakeRoute encoded messages and attestation digests from the EVM-generated JSON; do not independently recreate the fixture values.
- Replace the obsolete 16-byte RateUpdate fixture and e91f63a8... digest.
- Replace the locally constructed StakeRoute fixture with the authoritative EVM vector (currently digest 344f92bd..., subject only to an intentional vector regeneration).
- Include non-second-aligned millisecond endpoints so slot/second/millisecond interpretations cannot accidentally pass.
- Add negative tests for non-canonical hook lengths and malformed values.
- Run the full Aiken suite and verify byte-for-byte RFC1 message and keccak256 attestation-digest parity.

## Acceptance criteria

- V1.2 RC1 Aiken decodes the final 120-byte POSIX-ms RateUpdate schema.
- RateUpdate and StakeRoute fixtures are copied exactly from the committed EVM-generated vector file.
- Encoded message bytes and attestation digests match EVM byte-for-byte.
- RateUpdate rejects every hook length other than 120; StakeRoute rejects every hook length other than 64.
- Tests demonstrate non-zero millisecond components for both RateUpdate endpoints.
- No test or production path relies on the obsolete 16-byte RateUpdate layout or Shelley-slot semantics.

## References

- [#1567 — POSIX-ms RateUpdate decision and acceptance criteria](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/issues/1567)
- [#1564 — merged 120-byte rate-schedule implementation](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/pull/1564)
- [#1568 — merged authoritative 64-byte StakeRoute payload and vectors](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/pull/1568)
- [#1531 — Cardano staking bridge transitions and RFC1 parity requirements](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi/issues/1531)
- [spine PR #37 — rate-broadcast re-vendor work and review finding requiring POSIX-ms vectors](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi-cross-chain-spine/pull/37)
- [spine #24 — cross-chain native-staking parity acceptance criteria](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi-cross-chain-spine/issues/24)
- [spine #28 — automated three-way codec-parity gate](https://github.com/realfi-co/realfi-cross-chain-spine/issues/28)

tasks.description:
## Summary
`RealfiSDKV1_2Beta.create()` throws `ReferenceError: ScriptHash is not defined` while deriving the protocol scripts. The v1.2 **generated** types (`frontend/sdk/src/generated-types/v1_2_beta/index.ts`) dropped the `const ScriptHash = Type.String();` alias that `v1_1_rc1` declares (line 10), while keeping ~40 usages of it.

## Why it slipped
- The generated file is `// @ts-nocheck`, so the missing alias never surfaced at type-check time.
- The only existing v1.2 SDK test exercises the **codec/redeemer** — `create()` had never been run by any caller until the v1.2 Yaci deploy in #1596.

## Consumer-side patch already merged (#1596)
Commit `6daae5d0` restored the alias in the generated file to match `v1_1_rc1` (one line: `const ScriptHash = Type.String();`). Smoke-tested: all 13 script constructors `create()` builds succeed (13 ok, 0 failed).

## The durable fix (this issue)
The above is a hand-patch of a **generated** file — a regen will re-drop it. The fix belongs in the **codegen** so `ScriptHash` is always emitted for v1.2 (as it is for `v1_1_rc1`).

- File: `frontend/sdk/src/generated-types/v1_2_beta/index.ts` (generated)
- Ref: PR #1596, commit `6daae5d0`

tasks.title: fix(sdk): bridge-nonce init datum next must be 33-byte genesis_next sentinel (codegen source)
tasks.description:
## Summary
`mintBridgeNonceNFT` built the bridge-nonce init datum with `next = 0xff×32`, but the Aiken `genesis_next` sentinel is `0xff×33` (a value larger than any 32-byte nonce). `validate_bridge_nonce_init` checks the init datum for **exact** equality with `{ nonce: #"", next: 0xff×33, used: True }`, so the `bridge_nonce` mint validator crashed (`Mint[0] the validator crashed / exited prematurely`).

## Why it slipped
This path (`mintBridgeNonceNFT`) had never been exercised — the `bridge_nonce` bootstrap is first run by the v1.2 Yaci deploy in #1596.

## Consumer-side patch already merged (#1596)
Commit `9ab87b6e` in `frontend/sdk/src/sdk/v1_2_beta/index.ts` changed `next: "ff".repeat(32)` → `next: "ff".repeat(33)` to match the contract.

## The durable fix (this issue)
Confirm the `33` is correct against the `genesis_next` sentinel and ensure whatever generates/derives this datum encodes the 33-byte sentinel canonically (not a hard-coded literal that can drift from the `.ak` definition). If this value is or should be codegen-derived, fix it at the source so it can't diverge from the Aiken contract again.

- File: `frontend/sdk/src/sdk/v1_2_beta/index.ts` (`RealfiSDKV1_2Beta.mintBridgeNonceNFT`)
- Ref: PR #1596, commit `9ab87b6e`

tasks.title: Cardano BridgeOut producer for the sUSDr return leg — emit attested Transfer(5) (G4 other half)
tasks.description:
## Context

The **EVM half of the sUSDr return leg (G4) is shipped and proven live** — PR #1595 adds `RealFiRateReceiver` `EVENT_TRANSFER(5)` → `SUSDrStakingEntry.mintRelocation`, deployed to Sepolia via UUPS upgrade and verified end-to-end (a hand-attested sUSDr `Transfer(5)` minted 100 sUSDr 1:1, replay guard held — mint tx `0xeb7ac4c795fb92debb7897eda2cae8dede93fd5c5e9adf15a3d52efacf224b8c`).

The **other half is on Cardano**: a producer that burns sUSDr on the vault side and emits the attested `Transfer` (eventType 5) the EVM handler consumes. Until this exists, sUSDr only flows EVM→Cardano; the round-trip stays open.

## Scope

Cardano BridgeOut producer for the sUSDr return leg:
- Burn/relocate the sUSDr on the Cardano vault side (share token moves cross-chain alone — pure 1:1 relocation, no backing movement, no rate math; DEC-6 / STAKE-006).
- Emit an attested `Transfer` message that matches the **generic header codec** the EVM handler decodes — header-only, **no hookData**:
  - `eventType = 5` (Transfer), `assetId = 1` (sUSDr)
  - `sourceDomain = 10004` (Cardano), `destinationDomain = 1` (EVM hub)
  - **`recipient` @ offset 88** (32-byte, low 20 = EVM address), **`amount` @ offset 120**
  - (Same layout `USDrController` already consumes for USDr-in.)

## Dependency

This is `bridgeOut` applied to sUSDr — **depends on the SDK bridge-tx assembly (#1606)**. Once that lands, this is the sUSDr-asset instantiation of it plus the spine relaying the emitted message to EVM (spine G3, #39).

tasks.title: EVM redemption-liquidity redesign — order/request model in USDrMintController (mainnet-gating)
tasks.description:
## Summary

Redesign `USDrMintController` to **separate 1:1 valuation from redemption liquidity**. Valuation stays on-chain and immutable (1 USDr = 1 USDC = $1, landed in #1450 request 1); this changes only *liquidity/timing*. Redemption moves from a synchronous atomic payout to an **order/request model** that mirrors the already-audited-shape Cardano order model (`contracts/lib/v1_1_rc1/`).

**Mainnet-gating.** Modifies an already-deployed EVM trust surface, so it must be **in the frozen audit scope** for the EVM+spine audit (#1535). EVM-only build; Jan-independent (the Cardano reference model already exists in-repo).

## Problem

Today `mint()` pulls all USDC into the controller and `redeem()` pays out synchronously/atomically from the controller's own balance. There is no sweep/withdraw path, so reserves sit **100% idle**; and if capital were deployed productively, the controller would be mostly empty and `redeem()` would revert on the final transfer. We want capital deployed productively behind a liquidity buffer, without promising instant atomic redemption.

## Target model — order-based redemption (EVM mirror of Cardano `ORedeem`→`Execute`)

1. **Request (holder):** `requestRedemption(usdrAmount, minUsdcOut)` — holder's USDr is **escrowed** (pulled in, not burned); an `Order` is recorded `Pending`; `reserveBackedSupply` untouched; `RedemptionRequested` emitted.
2. **Execute (operator):** `executeRedemption(uint256[] ids)` `onlyRole(OPERATOR_ROLE)` — per order: burn escrowed USDr, transfer USDC to holder, enforce `usdcOut >= minUsdcOut`, decrement `reserveBackedSupply`/`reserveBackedUsdc`, mark `Executed`, report `BurnReport` to Cardano (Flow J). Batched; each order validated independently.
3. **Cancel (holder):** `cancelRedemption(uint256 id)` — holder reclaims escrow while `Pending`.
4. **Escape hatch (paused):** while `paused()`, holder can reclaim escrow on a `Pending` order even if cancel is otherwise gated (mirrors Cardano `Invalidated`).

State machine: `Pending → Executed` (operator) · `Pending → Cancelled` (holder cancel, or holder reclaim while paused).

This makes an intentionally mostly-empty pool safe: USDC only needs to be present when the operator chooses to execute a batch, and the operator only executes what it can fund.

## Contract-level changes (`eth/hardhat/contracts/usdr/USDrMintController.sol`)

- **`mint()`** — mostly unchanged (deposit USDC, mint 1:1); USDC no longer must stay locked.
- **`redeem()`** — synchronous atomic path **removed**, replaced by `requestRedemption` / `executeRedemption` / `cancelRedemption`.
- **Sweep / replenish** — `sweep(address to, uint256 amount)` + `replenish(uint256 amount)`, both `onlyRole(OPERATOR_ROLE)`, bounded by policy + event-logged.
- **New role** — `OPERATOR_ROLE` (attestor/operator multisig/timelock; ties custody spine#26/#29/#41 — build against a placeholder admin, rewire later).
- **New storage** — `Order` struct + `mapping(uint256 => Order) orders`, `uint256 nextOrderId`, `uint256 escrowedUsdr`. **Consume from `__gap` (currently `uint256[41]`); keep proxy layout stable.**
- **Events** — `RedemptionRequested`, `RedemptionExecuted`, `RedemptionCancelled`, `Swept`, `Replenished`.
- **Errors** — `NotOrderOwner`, `OrderNotPending`, `SlippageExceeded`, `UnknownOrder`, `SlippageFloorTooHigh`.

## Accounting / invariants

- `reserveBackedSupply` / `reserveBackedUsdc` / `escrowedUsdr` / `bufferUsdc` (on-chain) + `deployedUsdc` (attested, DEC-8 / thin-contract model).
- Escrowed USDr is held (not burned) → a cancel is a clean supply no-op; burn happens only on execute, coupled 1:1 with reserve movement.
- Solvency: `bufferUsdc + deployedUsdc >= reserveBackedUsdc`.
- `executeRedemption` keeps the hard guards that a redemption never releases more USDC than the reserve path took in (`reserveBackedUsdc`) nor burns more than `reserveBackedSupply` (`ExceedsReserveBacked`/`ExceedsReserveUsdc` move to execute).

## Open sub-decisions to close in this ticket

- **`minUsdcOut`** — RESOLVED: kept for Cardano parity/forward-compat; reject `minUsdcOut > usdrAmount` (`SlippageFloorTooHigh`) so an un-fulfillable floor can't grief an operator batch; execute-time floor stays belt-and-suspenders.
- **Cancel authority** — lean holder-only + paused escape hatch (matches Cardano; operator just declines to execute). Confirm.
- **Pending-order expiry** — lean no timer (Cardano has none); rely on cancel + paused hatch. Confirm.
- **Sweep/replenish bounds** — policy cap (must leave a buffer floor) vs pure attestor-discretion + event log. **Needs treasury input.**
- **Yield on deployed USDC** — accrues to protocol/treasury (USDr is not yield-bearing; sUSDr is the yield instrument). Confirm.
- **Scope** — order flow applies only to the institutional reserve-redeem path; `directMint` (fiat, no reserve leg) and sUSDr staking/cooldown are separate. Confirm.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Order-based `requestRedemption` / `executeRedemption` (batched) / `cancelRedemption` + paused reclaim implemented; synchronous `redeem()` removed.
- [ ] `OPERATOR_ROLE`-gated `sweep` / `replenish`.
- [ ] Storage added via `__gap`, proxy layout verified upgrade-safe.
- [ ] Invariants + guards enforced at execute; unit tests incl. cancel no-op-on-supply, paused reclaim, slippage-floor rejection, batch partial-fund.
- [ ] `BurnReport` → Cardano (Flow J) wired for executed orders.
- [ ] Open sub-decisions closed (treasury input on sweep bounds captured).
- [ ] Confirmed in the audit scope for #1535.

## References

- Design brief: `cross-chain/XC-EVM-redemption-liquidity-design.md` (design-locked 2026-07-13).
- Origin: Jan (j-mueller) review of #1450, request 2.
- Cardano model mirrored: `contracts/lib/v1_1_rc1/` (`burn.ak`, `validators/v1_1_rc1/order.ak`, `protocol_orchestrator.ak`).
- Mainnet-gating item; audit scope #1535.

## Summary

Stand up a **fresh `v1_2_beta` Cardano deployment on a persistent public testnet (Preview, or preprod)** using the **current merged contracts + the current attestor roster**, and run an **end-to-end flow**, recording the transaction hashes. Today the only persistent on-chain Cardano evidence is an **older** run.

- **EVM is deployed + proven on Sepolia (`v1_2_beta`)** with verifiable on-chain txs (G4 mint, loopback `MessageSent`/`receiveMessage`, sUSDr return-leg delivery).
- **Cardano only runs on ephemeral local Yaci** (fresh devnet per e2e run — no persistent address book / txs).
- The **only persistent Cardano on-chain evidence is the V1.1 RC1 Preview run in #1441** (`preview.cexplorer.io`) — it predates `v1_2_beta`, uses the old scripts + a different attestor, and its deploy environment is torn down (txs persist on-chain; the live UTxO set does not).
- So auditors have **no current, verifiable Cardano on-chain reference matching the code they'll audit**. This is the Cardano counterpart to the EVM Sepolia deployment.

## Ask / scope

1. Deploy the **current `v1_2_beta` Cardano contracts** to a **persistent public testnet** — **Preview** (preferred, matches #1441) or preprod.
2. Use the **current attestor roster**, kept consistent with the Sepolia transmitter's rotated key (single attestor, threshold 1 for now — same posture as EVM testnet).
3. Run an **end-to-end flow**: USDr mint → bridge-out/in (USDr) → stake → sUSDr bridge-out/in → unstake. Capture every submitted tx.

## Deliverables

- Network (preview vs preprod), **script addresses + hashes**, minting-policy IDs, the canonical **vault UTxO**, the **`bridge_nonce`** NFT.
- Data-provider endpoints used (Kupo / Ogmios / Blockfrost).
- The **e2e transaction list** with `preview.cexplorer.io` (or preprod explorer) links.
- Update `scope-of-works/reference-material/ENVIRONMENTS.md` §3.2/§3.3 with the above (currently marked TBD; the RC1 run is recorded there as the interim precedent).

## Notes / precedent

- #1441 already has the RC1 Preview run + the deployment tooling/driver — this is essentially a re-run on the current scripts + roster.
- Feeds the Cardano audit engagement (#1534) and the cross-chain reference package.
- Lane: **Cardano**.

tasks.title: Hand EVM admin/upgrade authority to a timelock/multisig (not the deployer EOA) before mainnet
tasks.description:
## Summary

Before the mainnet deploy, hand EVM **admin / upgrade authority off the deployer EOA** and onto a governance contract (timelock or multisig). This is the contract-ownership half of custody, distinct from attestor-key custody (spine#29).

## Current state
